newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends sharply down on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends sharply down on liquidation.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled sharply lower amid brisk and steady speculative liquidation, trading sources said.

The July contract closed 0.31 cent lower at 11.06 cents per lb, traded 11.38 to 11.05 cents. Most-active October ended down 0.30 cent at 11.03 cents, while the rest of the board settled 0.23 to 0.14 cent weaker.

The July/October switch closed at 0.03 cent from 0.05 cent on Thursday, after trading at par during the session. "I wouldn't be surprised to see another move lower before the market becomes oversold," a broker said.

Trading sources blamed losses on speculative rolling out of long July positions ahead expiry on June 30, and on liquidation in the most-active October contract. Some selling in the March contract was also cited.
Prices racked up losses early, drifted near the intraday for most of the session, and then fell to the day's lows just ahead of the close.
While short-covering by the trade held the market over support at 11.00 cents, both the July and October contracts are expected to take out the key level on Monday.
"We saw a small bounce but it really failed to get over significant numbers," a broker said. "With the weekend here and a huge spec long position, more speculators bailed out ahead of the close."

Open interest in the October contract rose 3,034 lots to stand at 89,486 lots before the open. July lost 4,613 lots but maintained a high open interest of 45,301 lots, with just seven trading days before the contract expires.
The October contract fell short of reaching a three-week low of 10.96 cents, hit on June 2. July just missed its recent low of 11.04 cents, reached on May 27.
An estimated 60,109 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 20,565 lots.
